THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though this matter is listed for admission, with consent of learned counsel for both parties, matter is taken up for final disposal.

2. Challenging judgment and award dated 29.07.2019 passed by III Addl. Senior Civil Judge and Addl. M.A.C.T., at Dharwad, in MVC no.825/2016, this appeal is filed by claimant for enhancement of compensation.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. Brief facts as stated are that on 26.04.2016, when Srinivas D. was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-26/V-8147, on Nargund-Konnur road, driver of lorry bearing registration no.KA-29/A-2120 drove it in rash and negligent manner and dashed to motorcycle from behind,
causing his death on spot.
4. Alleging loss of dependency, his mother filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, against owner and insurer of offending vehicle.
5. On service of summons, owner and insurer filed separate objections opposing claim petition.

Negligence in causing accident was alleged against deceased and sought for dismissal of claim petition.
6.

Insurer contended that its liability was subject to issuance of insurance policy, possession of valid permit, fitness certificate in respect of lorry and valid driving licence by driver as on date of accident.
7. Thereafter, Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence of claimant as PW.1 and got marked Exhibits P1 to P15.

Respondents examined one witness as RW1 and got marked Exhibits R1 to R6.
8.

On consideration, tribunal held that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver, insurance policy issued with respect to said vehicle was valid on date of accident and Lakshmibayi W/O Dharmaraj More vs Smt.Rashmi W/O Hajimohammed ... on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120006797/

 9.
Not satisfied with quantum of compensation, claimant is in appeal for enhancement.
10. Sri Harish S. Nayak, learned counsel appearing for claimant-appellant sought enhancement of compensation.
It was submitted that deceased Srinivas was working as Mechanic in 'Jyothi Engineering Works' and earning Rs.10,000/- p.m., and tribunal erred in taking it at Rs.7,000/-.
It was submitted that tribunal failed to consider future prospects, relying upon decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Pranay Sethi Vs. National Insurance co. Ltd. 1 11.

entities.text: Pranay Sethi Vs. National Insurance co. Ltd. 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On other hand, Sri. G. N.Raichur, learned counsel for insurer supported award.
It was submitted that on overall consideration, compensation awarded was adequate and sought dismissal of appeal.

12. From above submission and since only claimant is in appeal for enhancement of compensation,
only point that arises for consideration is:
A I R 20 1 7 S C 5 1 5 7 "Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
13.
Insofar as income, though claimant stated that deceased was aged 31 years, working as mechanic and earning Rs.10,000/- per month, no specific evidence is led to substantiate same.
In absence, it has to be assessed on notional terms.
Notional income for year 2016 as per norms adopted by Karnataka Legal Services Committee for settlement of cases before Lok Adalath is Rs.8,750/-.
Thus tribunal was not justified in considering lower monthly income.
Therefore, Rs.8750/- has to be taken as monthly income.
14. Admittedly deceased was aged 31 years, and self-employed.
Claim petition is filed by his mother as sole dependent.

As per decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi's case (supra),
multiplier applicable will be '16', addition of future prospects will have to be at '40%' and deduction towards personal expenses will have to be at ''.

Thus, loss of dependency would be as follows:

. Insofar as rate of interest, this Court in case of Shriram General Insurance Company Limited, Rajasthan V/s Smt.Laxmi and others 2 has held rate of interest awardable in a claim petition arising under Motor Vehicles Act has to be at 6% per annum.

16. Point for consideration is thus answered partly in affirmative.

Consequently following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
ii. Claimant is held entitled for reassessed compensation of Rs.12,53,000/- as against Rs.7,52,000/- awarded by tribunal, with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit.
iii. Insurer is directed to deposit enhanced compensation within six weeks.

iv. On deposit, tribunal to release sum of Rs.1,25,000/- and keep remaining in fixed deposit in any nationalized bank initially for a period of three years.
